text:
mira: Quick sanity check — Ark9B-int4 bring-up numbers landed. Unit econ looks promising (~0.28x cost vs baseline), but we see a quality drop on longform summarization and some edge-case Q&A slices. Can we do a short cost-vs-quality summary + a recommended routing/holdback plan for GTN? attaching quick perf samples below.
ash: Posted the microbench numbers earlier: throughput 220 tok/s/GPU, median p95 latency 420ms for 1k context on our test infra. Cost per 1M tokens (est): $18 (int4) vs $64 (baseline int8->larger 13b). Rough ballpark.
mira: Sample quality diffs from eval harness (50k sample mix):
- short chat (customer-support): delta ROUGE(-0.3) / accept rate -0.5%
- longform summarization (3-6 paragraphs): BLEU-like surrogate -3.8 / human flagged regressions 4.7%
- factual Q&A (open-domain): exact-match -1.6% / hallucination uptick on multi-hop examples
gordon: Noted runtime caveat: Ark9B-int4 has smaller KV footprint but worse kvcache hit stability for multi-turn due to quantization-induced activations noise. On long sequences we see extra kv-evictions -> tail latency spikes on 2% of requests. Batching helps but increases median latency slightly.
kai: For GTN ask: product wants clear guidance — is this "fast + mostly fine" or "risky for longform"? Also need a short blurb we can send to the GTN PMs about expected user experience and recommended safeguards.
ash: Quick econ summary (rounded):
- Unit cost multiplier vs baseline = 0.28x
- Expected token savings per 100k daily active users (DAU) if migrated = ~
  - 100k DAU * 1k tokens/day * (1 - 0.28) = ~72M tokens/day saved -> ~$1.3k/day ($39k/mo) on service L0 pricing assumptions
- Ops impact: slightly higher QA overhead for longform slices; monitoring signal needs to be tightened.
mira: Mini scorecard (from signal slices):
```
Model: Ark9B-int4
Slices: short-chat | longform-summary | factual-qa
Quality delta vs baseline: -0.5% | -3.8% | -1.6%
Latency (p95 1k ctx): 420ms | 560ms (kv tail) | 430ms
Unit-cost: 0.28x baseline
Recommended product-risk: Low | Medium-High | Medium
```
sam: Product ask: If we route 50% of traffic to Ark9B-int4, how many false-negatives/human flags do we expect for longform? Numbers matter for GTN risk tolerance.
mira: Back-of-envelope: longform flagged at 4.7% on our eval slice. If 50% routed, extra flagged = 0.5 * 4.7% * longform-traffic-share. If longform is 8% of total requests -> extra flagged ~0.188% absolute increase in total volume (~1.9 flags per 1k requests). We should present both relative and absolute counts to GTN.
gordon: Ops mitigations: implement kvcache pinning for canary hosts, enable small intra-request retry on tail lat spikes, and add a slice-specific alert (longform_regressions > 2% in 1h).
kai: Proposed rollout plan for GTN messaging and safe deployment:
1) Canary 5% of total traffic, restricted to low-risk short-chat and code/FAQ slices only.
2) Shadow 20% longform traffic for 48h (collect human-in-the-loop labels).
3) If slice regressions < 2% and user-visible complaints low, expand to 25% for general low-latency slices.
4) Keep 0% or small holdback (5%) for longform until human sample improvement to <2%.
5) Auto-fallback: any request where regression detector score > threshold -> route to baseline model (config flag `route_on_regression: true`).
ash: Ops config snippet we recommend for rollout:
```
canary:
  percent: 5
  allowed_slices: [short-chat, faq, code]
shadow:
  percent: 20
  slice: longform-summary
fallback_policy:
  threshold_regression_score: 0.72
  fallback_model: baseline-13b-int8
```
sam: That plan is good. For GTN PR we need a one-line recommendation + a risk table. Can you give that? I'll draft messaging.
mira: One-line: "Ark9B-int4 reduces per-token cost by ~72% with small regressions on short chat and measurable regression on longform; recommend conservative rollout with longform holdback until additional evals complete."
Risk table (short):
- Cost upside: High (~0.28x unit cost)
- Short-chat impact: Negligible
- Longform impact: Noticeable (4.7% flags) -> Require holdback/shadowing
- Ops burden: Moderate (monitoring + kvcache tuning)
gordon: I'll add the alerts and pinning config. ops-bot will create the canary env later today.
ops-bot: Canary deployment env created: canary-ark9b-2026-03-23. Runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/ark9b-canary
kai: Final ask: can we produce a 1-page slide for GTN with the scorecard + rollout plan by EOD? If yes we'll coordinate PM announcement.
mira: Yes — I'll do the slide and include the mini-scorecard numbers and the absolute flag counts. Will ping when ready. :thumbsup
